related_resources.reason: Contemporary five-author discovery paper, received 9 February 1968 and published 24 February; original discussion left neutron-star versus white-dwarf interpretations open.
Firsthand recollection of the array and chart analysis, discovery sequence, media questions, Nobel response, gamma/X-ray careers; retrospective after-dinner talk, not a verbatim 1967 diary.
First-person interviews and archival plot captions: 6 August anomaly, 28 November pulse recording, independent telescope timing issue, LGM shorthand and 2018 award.
Technical discovery chronology, scintillation search and publication as understood in retrospective professional history.
Belfast and Lurgan biography, Mount School, Glasgow 1965 graduation, Cambridge degree date in institutional record, later recognition.
First-person recollection of architect father, astronomical book, marriage and part-time research appointments, interests beyond science.
Sex-segregated science education, Glasgow lecture-hall experience, graduate circumstances, scholarship origins.
Quaker family and school background as a community account; use for self-identified faith, not inference about the causal origins of her scientific results.
Institutional citation describing radio, gamma, X-ray and infrared/mm astronomy, JCMT role, Open University astronomy group, leadership, Athena SWAN and access initiatives.
Professional history, election as FRS 2003, leadership, 2010 Faraday Prize, 2015 Royal Medal, Copley award; profile includes some stale current-appointments text.
2021 Copley, direct personal statement about work on binary stars, building telescopes, scientific leadership and support for graduate students.
Exact division of recognized work: Ryle aperture synthesis, Hewish decisive role in pulsar discovery. The record cannot itself establish reasons for not including other participants.
2018 award, its stated rationale and Bell Burnell’s intended donation to UK/Ireland Institute of Physics doctoral support.
Source dated 15 July 2026: reports 54 scholars supported since foundation of the programme in 2019; this is a dated count, not a permanent total.
Mullard Space Science Laboratory and Ariel V details, school barriers and Athena SWAN participation; modern institutional retrospective.
Physical interpretation of highly magnetized rotating neutron stars, beamed emission, period range and role as astrophysical clocks.
Radio-wave propagation through plasma, frequency-dependent time delay, dispersion-measure definitions and correctly unitized formula.
History of the Hulse–Taylor binary pulsar as a later, separate scientific discovery and application of pulsar timing.
University career, childhood and education, recognition and later leadership as public institutional biography.
Career transitions, experience with part-time jobs after marriage, Open University work, and donation in her own words.
Only public abstract inspected. The full article was not read; not the basis for detailed claims about childhood or private life.
University’s official 2018 announcement of chancellorship.
University list documents Bell Burnell serving as chancellor 2018–2023, avoiding stale claims of current office.
1934 original theoretical proposal linking supernovae to neutron stars; does not imply their predictions were observationally verified then.
Retrospective account of Hoyle criticizing the Nobel prize committee over omission of Jocelyn Bell Burnell; treat journalistic interpretation and speculation as such.
History of CP1919 / PSR B1919+21, Crab pulsar identification, and interpretation of pulsed radio measurements.
MSSL located at Holmbury St Mary, Dorking, Surrey, rather than central London.
